edits.text: 1) Does what follows the cut overturn, negate, limit, or materially change the claim made so far?  - In addition to the existing guidance, treat any cut as high-risk (raise contra sharply toward 1.0 and lower cohesion toward 0) whenever the remainder supplies material that the left fragment needs to be true or complete: the main-clause verb or complement, an essential result or ordinal that completes a partial outcome, the last item of an enumerated result list, a final negation, or the temporal/modal frame that scopes the left fragment. Concretely: if the left fragment, read alone, would assert a concrete result/role/measurement/ordinal or would leave a predicate or list visibly unfinished, then the remainder is semantically required and the cut should be penalized accordingly. Only when the remainder merely adds optional descriptive detail (not needed to complete or to rescue the truth of the left fragment) should you apply the usual graded probability estimate for contra.
